children: Japan's 30-year government bond sale signals investor caution amid persistent fiscal concerns. As bond prices fall when yields rise, the record 4.1% highest accepted yield at Thursday's auction shows that buyers demanded steep discounts--and higher returns--to take on long-term debt risks. Other measures of demand also deteriorated from the previous sale in August. The tail, or the difference between the average and lowest accepted prices, widened to 0.28 from 0.21, while the bid-to-cover ratio fell to 3.79 from 3.86. Super-long-zone investors are likely to remain cautious as details of the next fiscal year's budget are expected to unfold, analysts say. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)
